title: Phonon-limited resistivity of Pb, Nb and Al with thermal expansion and TDEP anharmonicity
source: A. Wang, J. Yin, F. A. Goudreault, M. Cote, O. Hellman, S. Ponce (2026), Materials Cloud Archive record zxf0b-rs406 (DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:4h-r1), CC BY 4.0. Retrieved author calculations; no new EPW calculation is run.
archive_readme:
#################################################################################################################################################
# Antagonistic impact of thermal expansion and phonon anharmonicity on the phonon-limited resistivity of elemental metals from first principles
#################################################################################################################################################
# A. Wang, J. Yin, F. Goudreault, M Côté, O. Hellman, and S. Poncé

## (1) Calculation software:
We use two versions of QE (QE v7.3 with EPW v5.8, and QE v7.4 with EPW v5.9), and each has two branches (one is the unchanged code, named qe-7.3 and qe-7.4, one is modified by us to make the TDEP output force readable, named qe-7.3-tdep and qe-7.4-tdep).

The unchanged QE code can be downloaded from [github.com/QEF/q-e/qe-7.3](https://github.com/QEF/q-e/tree/qe-7.3) and [github.com/QEF/q-e/qe-7.4](https://github.com/QEF/q-e/tree/qe-7.4).

The method to modify the code is given in the file `./data_for_paper/software`

## (2) Band structure and phonon property calculations with and without thermal expansion:
In files `./data_for_paper/Al(Nb, Pb)/1-pw/band-structure/` and `./data_for_paper/Al(Nb, Pb)/2-ph/`,
we give the input and output files for the electron band and phonon calculations with lattice parameters in different temperatures.
This part we use the qe-7.3 code.

After the phonon calculation, use `python pp.py` to get the "save" file.
Copy the espresso.xml into this file, and rename it to be ifc.q2r.xml.
Copy the matdyn*.xml into the save file and rename to Al.dyn_q*.xml/Nb.dyn_q*.xml/Pb.dyn_q*.xml.

## (3) Phonon calculations include anharmonicity with TDEP:
In files `./data_for_paper/Al(Nb, Pb)/3-ph-anharm-TDEP/`, we do the TDEP iterations at different temperatures to
calculate the interatomic force constants (IFCs) that include the phonon anharmonicity.

The calculation procedure is given in the file `./data_for_paper/Al(Nb, Pb)/3-ph-anharm-TDEP/README.md`.
After the calculations, we get the "updated_qe.fc.xml" file in `./data_for_paper/Al(Nb, Pb)/3-ph-anharm-TDEP/*K/sampling.*k/iter.00*/matdyn/` of different temperatures.

Copy the "save" files in `./data_for_paper/Al(Nb, Pb)/2-ph/ph-*K/`, and rename it to be "save-*K".
Then, copy the "updated_qe.fc.xml" file into the "save-*K" and rename it to be ifc.q2r.xml.
Now, we have the "save-*K" file including the TDEP IFCs for the EPW calculation.

Note that in `./data_for_paper/Pb/3-ph-anharm-TDEP/0K-alat/`, we also need to calculate the TDEP at 210, 410, and 610 K with lattice parameter without thermal expansion.
Copy the three "updated_qe.fc.xml" files into `./data_for_paper/Pb/2-ph/ph-0K/save-210K(save-410K, save-610K)` and rename it to be ifc.q2r.xml.

## (4) EPW calculation with/wo TE, with/wo phonon anharmonicity:
In files `data_for_paper/Pb(Al, Nb)/4-epw`, we do the EPW calculations to obtain the electrical resistivity.
All the inputs and outputs are given.
In subdirectory `1-DFPT` and `2-with_TE`, we use the qe-7.3. Moreover, the original "save" file is the input.

In files `3-anharm` and `4-TE_and_anharm` for Pb and `3-TE_and_anharm` for Al and Nb, we use the qe-7.3-tdep.
Note that in these files, apart from the code, we also need to read the "save-*K" file.

## (5) Spectral decomposition of the electron scattering rates calculation:
In files `./data_for_paper/Pb/4-epw/1-DFPT/epw/spec/`, use the "run" file provided and qe-7.4, we can calculate the spectral decomposition
of the electron scattering rates of Pb in 610 K without TE or anharmonicity.

In files `./data_for_paper/Pb/4-epw/2-with_TE/610K/spec/`, with the "run" file provided and qe-7.4, we can calculate the spectral decomposition
of the electron scattering rates of Pb in 610 K with TE.

In files `./data_for_paper/Pb/4-epw/4-TE_and_anharm/610K/spec/`, with the "run" file provided and qe-7.4-tdep,
we can calculate the spectral decomposition of the electron scattering rates of Pb in 610 K with TE and anharmonicity.

methods.electrons: Quantum ESPRESSO 7.3 (Pb: fully relativistic LDA with spin-orbit coupling; Al, Nb: see the archived inputs). One atom per primitive cell: Pb and Al fcc, Nb bcc.
methods.phonons: DFPT on an 8x8x8 (Pb) or 6x6x6 (Al, Nb) q-grid, force constants from q2r; TDEP (stochastic self-consistent sampling with quantum statistics at the stated temperature, see the archive README) converted to the same q2r format. The electron-phonon deformation potentials always come from DFPT at the run's lattice parameter; the force constants (DFPT or TDEP) set the phonon frequencies and eigenvectors.
methods.transport: EPW (v5.8) linearised Boltzmann equation for the phonon-limited conductivity on fine k and q meshes, with adaptive smearing; each output prints the self-energy relaxation-time (SERTA) solution followed by the iterations of the full iterative solution (IBTE).
methods.lattice_parameter_note: Temperature-dependent lattice parameters from the authors (thermal expansion); the 0 K value is the static relaxed lattice.

transport.returns: the run's input parameters, lattice parameter, fine meshes and, for each temperature, the Fermi level, printed DOS, SERTA conductivity tensor, IBTE iteration history and final IBTE conductivity tensor, in (Ohm cm)^-1

phonons.returns: harmonic frequencies (meV) of that force-constant set on a Gamma-centred n^3 grid (q folded into the first Brillouin zone, Cartesian, units of 2 pi / alat), optionally the polarisation vectors, a DOS histogram, standard DOS moments and the dispersion along high-symmetry lines; computed by the lab (numpy Fourier interpolation with the simple acoustic sum rule, identical to matdyn.x)
